title: Secrets of Strixhaven Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "The great thrill of perfection is that we'll always be chasing it."
"The best answers leave you with more questions."
"War begets war. We may hope for peace, but it is only ever a brief interlude between bloody ages." —Plargg, dean of chaos
"If they will not listen to reason, drown them in nonsense." —Embrose, dean of shadow
The hunters came for the mushrooms. The trudges came for the mushroom hunters.
Seek inspiration at your own risk.
"We've all been broken and had to put ourselves back together with the pieces that were left." —Kequia Akosa
Once they were given a taste of bone they wouldn't touch anything else.
"The bites and scratches are worth it."
"Life is beauty and cruelty. Pain and joy. It is the promise of certain death at the end of a glorious journey." —Beledros Witherbloom
A neglected corner of the Adumbral Gardens, used by pages and diplomats seeking solitude for reflection and intrigue.
"I won't leave my students without a guide."
"When you find an equation that works, all that's left is finding its many applications." —Zimone
"I come up here to practice. You can see the entire Garden twisting reality. It's inspiring."
Ulna Alley is a maze of market stalls where anything can be purchased for the right price.
He'd practiced his scales specifically for this moment.
Students working in the field for the first time learn the benefits of small, agile spirit statues over large, strong ones.
"Adrix and I have always debated for the betterment of our students. That won't change now we're both deans."
To control a spell, you must first strip it of its flesh and bones.
Styluses are tools used by students to channel their magic. For young Quandrix mages, they can help navigate difficult calculations and focus perspective.
Hidden across Arcavios are great sculptures chiseled by the claws of Galazeth Prismari himself.
The Arch Obscura never appears for the same eyes twice. Those who bear witness either find peace in their own insignificance or dread in the unnatural twilight.
The mana currents around Spectacle Summit are so thoroughly infused with Prismari patterns that a simple drumbeat is enough to make them whirl in response.
"Where others see melancholy, I see promise. All our kindness and cruelty make such haunting poetry." —Shadrix Silverquill
"The Multiverse itself is a never-ending act of creation. Do not look inward so often that you forget how to see it." —Galazeth Prismari
"Respect for the past is respect for oneself. It's an admission that we too shall pass into history." —Velomachus Lorehold
"Existence is more perfect, more informative and unknowable, than the cleverest theorem ever devised." —Tanazir Quandrix
"Conflict guided our lives and placed blades in our hands. Even after death, we know nothing else."
The Dragonsguard ensures peace across Arcavios. Where peace is not possible, they ensure justice.
"There's so much to learn. Sometimes I wish there were more of me."
Omenpaths bring new students and new tactics to the field.
"Anyone who says a textbook can't end on a cliffhanger has never read volume one of *Finite Lattice Representation*!"
"Victory is nonnegotiable."
"Keep them in terrariums? No way! Snakes are meant to roam free, my friend."
"Behind every poised smile lies a seed of insecurity. Identify it, and you can exploit it." —Embrose, dean of shadow
"You must decide what you're willing to give to your spell craft: mana, pest essence, even your own life force. Everything is fair game for a resourceful mage." —Willowdusk
"STAY ON THE STAGE!" —Notices posted during Summitfest
"Have I finally done it? Have I finally freed myself from failure?"
"Why would I deprive the crowd of an encore?"
Each Strixhaven graduate receives a class ring bearing the university's motto: "Through study, know the world; through magic, know yourself."
"What drives the star arches to appear, and what causes them to sometimes disappear? I doubt even the Dawning Archaic knows." —Jadzi, Oracle of Arcavios
Knowledge is wasted if not shared.
The first sight most students see are the Torches of Enlightenment, welcoming them to the beginning of their great adventure.
The barest taste of Eldrazi power shatters both realms and identities.
"United, our roar will level mountains."
Infinitely powerless.
By the second night after the kami had drifted into town, the local general store was completely sold out of earplugs.
"May the memory of our fallen heroes ensnare the violent hearts of lesser men." —Great Threshold of Monserkat inscription
"Duty and law are the foundation on which civilization stands. They must not fall, for when they do, they take everything with them." —Lord Konda
She reaches beyond the physical realm, touching the ideals from which all creatures draw their power.
"Your unsolicited words enrich us all. Please, continue." —Yold, professor of cryptorelicology
"It's us against the world. Forever."
Crime doesn't pay nearly as well as the Agency.
A lifetime of keeping up appearances is not enough to earn an eternity of rest.
Strixhaven's five colleges encourage rivalries among the students, but some bonds transcend all barriers.
"There is always more to give."
The shield of unimpeachable purity is as strong as any wrought on the anvil.
"As this conflict grows, it gets harder to prevent the city from breaking down. How much longer can we keep this machinery balanced?"
"The realm of the gods opens before me!"
A blazing sun that never sets.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."
"The Ancestor saved us for a purpose."
"Your father was a dear friend to whom I owe much. He wanted me to look after you, to care for you should something happen to him."
The spear thrown by Kytheon's own hand was the weapon that felled his friends.
"The first griffins were made by the gods to capture falling stars; they were given the keenest eyes and the swiftest wings, and sent to keep watch above the clouds." —*The Cosmogony*
His oath required no service beyond death, but his honor demanded it.
"There shall be a vast shout and then a vaster silence." —Oracle *en-*Vec
The militia formed up in the central plaza awaiting the onslaught, but the giants never quite made it.
Some emeritus professors return from their wanderings periodically to share tales of the mystical wonders of Arcavios.
Another imminent battle subsided in busy snuffling and carefree rooting.
"No fact escapes me. Why do you think you can?"
The stronger the will, the more bewitching the song.
"Your proofs were a bit nontraditional, but effective nonetheless. Full marks."
"We've merged your life essence with that of several creatures at once. You're welcome." —Speaker Trifon
Critics were struck first by the elemental's surprising grace, and then by its fists.
"Every thought is a star illuminating the darkness. Inspiration comes from finding the constellations that link them."
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.
"There exists a theoretical infinity between the discrete atoms of reality. I'm simply appropriating that infinity as storage space."
Pests feed on carrion, mud, and one another.
"Vanya Falkenrath's paintings are astonishing. How does she manage to achieve such rich crimson hues?" —Stefan, art critic
Crippling fear precedes it. A foul stench accompanies it. Death follows in its wake.
From the echoes of a violent life, a terrible foe is born.
Ancient evils dwell within the burning chasm called the Ashmouth, ever ready to devour those foolish enough to travel alone.
"Rise, my pretty thing. Why rot in the river when you can serve at my bidding?"
On Innistrad, one person's windfall usually starts with another person lying face down in the mud.
"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?" —Vraska
Strixhaven forbade all magic from the Blood Age, so that is where Extus began his research.
The Orzhov are not the only religious tradition on Ravnica, nor the oldest.
"All things will fall to the Zero Point. By accepting this truth, my path is known and my fate is certain."
Some Strixhaven study groups are more welcoming than others.
In matters of life and death, he trusts his gut.
Many hands for many evils.
"The time for subtlety is over, darling."
"Eldrazi? Ha! Try walking through Zulaport at night with your pockets full. Now *that's* dangerous."
The desert is a voracious beast, devouring both flesh and stone.
"Molten earth has no anger of its own. Only by infusing it with your own rage can the magma seethe and take shape." —Koth of the Hammer
"Unimaginable riches? I assure you, I have a *vivid* imagination."
In the early days of Valley, desperate animalfolk harnessed the power of Calamity Beasts in ways that destroyed more than defended.
It was just another day on Innistrad.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.
"Blink or don't. You'll get hit either way."
"Some goblins are expendable. Some are impossible to get rid of. But he's both—at the same time!" —Starke
A captured elemental makes for a potent, albeit unstable, power source.
Seeing it coming a mile away is little comfort if you can't get out of range in time.
The ground erupted in time with the hedron's thrum, a dirge of the last days.
"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them." ―Euphemia, Nexus watcher
As subtle as a bogbeast —Witherbloom expression meaning "crude and clumsy"
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
"Life grows everywhere. My kin merely find those places where it grows strongest." —Nissa Revane
Its blood is life. Its body is growth.
The key is to slay it before it sprouts so many heads that your fear outpaces your greed.
After years of research, he finally unlocked the formula for the perfect punch.
"Naga shed their scales. We wear ours with pride." —Golran, dragonscale captain
Nashi knelt reverently before the kami and envisioned his family reunited.
Pharika has written her secrets on its bones so that only the worthy may discover them.
From the cracks in the stone, she reads stories of the past. From the swirling vines, she glimpses visions of the future.
Silent as a snowdrift. Inexorable as an avalanche.
A thousand years of history undone by one juvenile prank.
The shaman looked at the world through Ghalta's eyes and understood that everything else was his prey.
He'd chosen a sunlit clearing with open skies and an ample brook. All that remained was to find a worthy sapling.
"Regrowth is as inevitable as the tragedy that necessitates it."
Many an ancient treasure has been reduced to jagged caltrops by its snapping jaws.
Those who love the woods only wish to spread its majesty.
"Sure, trudges smell like soggy death, but the mushrooms on their backs are the tastiest delicacy in Sedgemoor!" —Gyome, Witherbloom chef
"When they write songs about this battle, I will make sure your name is forgotten, devil."
Sorin had created Avacyn, so it was a cruelty beyond imagining, a pain beyond description, that it fell upon him to end her forever.
"Not just any floriculturist can grow this caliber of nightbloom. We're looking for a rooftop hothouse with quite particular conditions." —Dr. A of the Foundway Associates
"A regression to ancient forms? A glimpse of future evolutions? Or a fleeting alteration of the present?" —Vorel of the Hull Clade
"Great power requires great sacrifice. But it need not be my own."
No one ever asked what was in Dina's concoctions, so long as they worked.
"I've heard enough."
"Hush now. I need your beauty sleep."
"At first, the equations were simply numbers. But in those numbers I saw a story, and in that story I saw a pattern, and suddenly it all fit together!"
Prismari students dance in the tension between passion and perfection.
"Your defiance is amusing, little mage. It's time you learn how fragile you really are." —Extus Narr
Havoc is a small price to pay for data.
Silverquill's elite know how to offer a scathing rebuttal without uttering a word.
"When your father is Dean Embrose, second best really isn't an option."
The clicks and buzz of the undercity proclaim him the incarnation of decay.
"The heroes of the past nourish our spirits by their example—and nourish our crops by their decay." —Jeddeg, philosopher of graves
"Death is my life's work."
"A fine example of addition by subtraction." —Deekah, professor of fractal theory
"The secrets of our world will be mine."
"Every life has a story to tell. I won't let them be forgotten."
Torn from history. Torn from memory. Torn from reality.
"Art is never finished. Merely abandoned."
"Only novice mages burn their whiskers. So pay attention!"
"The streets of Ravnica were stifling. Eldraine is an endless adventure paved in gold."
"Whoever summoned that thing had better confess right this moment, or the whole class will be cleaning the ink receptacles for a month!"
Her new demonic overlords prized her knowledge of Bant's landscape.
"What are they complaining about? It's not like axiomatic leyline paratrigonometrics is hard."
Automated units are deployed to stabilize merge sites deemed too dangerous even for trained intercessors.
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
"They're easy enough to squish, but they're a pain to wash out of a workbench." —Tergel, goblin explosioneer
When you spend most of your time running for your life, it pays to invest in quality footwear.
The toymaker frowned in bewilderment. None of his creations had ever sneezed before.
"We have barely begun to learn the secrets of the Fourth People. Every remnant of their presence, however cryptic, is a gift." —Akal Pakal, First Steward of Oteclan
With thistle, quill, twig, and beak, the finest artisans of each animalfolk society stitched unique quilts, patched together as a symbol of harmony.
Do not be so caught up in keeping track of time that you forget to make use of it.
Cast out of Garenbrig for his crimes, Ennor turned to fae magic to fashion the perfect weapon for his revenge.
"Good ideas don't take time. They take a lot of bad ideas first." —Ral Zarek
"You'll never get to the top if you don't know who's already there." —Kaya
Persecuted alchemists fled deep into Kessig's wilds, seeking solitude to continue their ghoulish craft.
"As Terisiare's mines ran dry, scrap metal became increasingly plentiful." —*The Antiquities War*
Travelers bathe in the falls to wash away curses from the pucas who lurk nearby.
After years of silence, the caves once again echo with the grisly sounds of Phyrexians preparing for war.
The sunlight falls pristine on the temple at Epityr, softened by the remembered shadows of angelic saviors' wings.
Silence, the poetry of a whispering wind, the centurial fall of tar on pale sand.
"When you can't find your way home, find home where you can." —Rho, veteran hero
Stability and volatility churn together, creating beauty and danger both.
Evendo's microbial life swiftly adapted to metabolize the leaking star fuel, devouring it like any other nourishment.
"Do not linger in such places, child. There the gwyllions dance. If they find you, you will join in their revels for eternity." —Talara, elvish safewright
At full moon, the river seeps over its banks and crawls through the woods like a blanket of serpents.
A smoldering storm of chilling fire.
A seething locus of reverent rage.
Iridescent debris and chromatic chemical fires litter Kavaron with the beauty of destruction.
"I love what they've done with the place." —Liliana Vess
Some of the nature spirits and wraiths that haunt Urborg take offense at the term "ghost town."
If it can't be had here, it can't be had on any world.
"Our ancestors brought down a Phyrexian portal ship, then built our town on its hull. We're pretty proud of that." —Alene of Riverspan
Serra's blessing lies strongest upon Sursi, where her holy chapels are untouched even as evil encroaches.
"The sylex blast marked not only the end of the war, but the end of Dominaria as most knew it." —*The Antiquities War*
Mage-students obsessed with the secrets of the past choose Lorehold, the college of archaeomancy.
Though dangerous, Shiv teems with both life and mana, making it a tempting destination for ambitious mages.
A hungry lair of flourishing rot.
Still to the ignorant eye, yet bursting with life. A million actions and reactions, unstoppable as the dawn.
Mage-students who see spellcraft as the highest form of expression choose Prismari, the college of elemental arts.
Mage-students who see the beauty in patterns and equations choose Quandrix, the college of numeromancy.
"The Tapestry weaves worlds on its own. All we do is tend to the process." —Antioxa, Drix elder
A forest that never thirsts always flourishes.
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
Hobs bury their kin far from home. They believe the dry, open ground keeps hags from stealing the bones and gwyllions from stealing the spirits.
Everyone is welcome in the floating Serran cities, though few but the most faithful attempt the ascent.
A flickering beacon of righteous corruption.
The boiling seas around Shiv provided a welcome layer of protection for the reclaimed Mana Rig.
Mage-students drawn to the power of language choose Silverquill, the college of eloquence.
Lorwyn contains many such places: not bustling, not frenetic, but teeming with life in their own, quiet way.
"We have inherited the mysteries of the Thran, but few of the answers." —Jhoira
Even the poisoned land around the Stronghold blossomed with new life in the wake of the Great Mending.
Majesty rising above the arid sweep of land, a bulwark horizon against the mundane, a divide cleaving inspiration from stagnation.
Many of Terisiare's islands are merely extensions of the root system of the Yavimaya magnigoth forests.
Those who bring nothing to the temple take nothing away.
As their roots soaked in a weak tea of bogwater and decay, the trees absorbed the essence of death into their living tissue.
"New things need room to grow. We prune time so the future can flourish." —Antioxa, Drix elder
A verdant paradox of primal logic.
Life and death mixing together, both ends of the same cycle giving rise to something else.
A figure is moved on a map, and the tide of war changes.
Mage-students fascinated by the energies of life and death choose Witherbloom, the college of essence studies.
"They never found the body of young Josu, or that of his murderous sister." —"The Fall of the House of Vess"
As magnigoth trees expanded across the sea into Almaaz and New Argive, it became clear Yavimaya's borders were never confined by its coastline.
